1. Nat Neurosci. 2008 Jul;11(7):834-42. doi: 10.1038/nn.2149. Epub 2008 Jun 15.

A disproportionate role for the fornix and mammillary bodies in recall versus 
recognition memory.

Tsivilis D(1), Vann SD, Denby C, Roberts N, Mayes AR, Montaldi D, Aggleton JP.

Author information:
(1)School of Psychological Sciences, Zochonis Building, University of 
Manchester, Brunswick Street, Manchester, M13 9PL, UK. 
dimitris.tsivilis@manchester.ac.uk

Uncovering the functional relationship between temporal lobe amnesia and 
diencephalic amnesia depends on determining the role of the fornix, the major 
interlinking fiber tract. In this study relating fornix volume with memory, we 
made magnetic resonance imaging-based volume estimates of 13 brain structures in 
38 individuals with surgically removed colloid cysts. Fornix status was assessed 
directly by overall volume and indirectly by mammillary body volume (which 
atrophies after fornix damage). Mammillary body volume significantly correlated 
with 13 out of 14 tests of episodic memory recall, but correlated poorly with 
recognition memory. Furthermore, as the volumes of the left fornix and the left 
mammillary bodies decreased, the difference between recall and recognition 
scores increased. No other structure was consistently associated with memory. 
These findings support models of diencephalic memory mechanisms that require 
hippocampal inputs for recall, but not for key elements of recognition.
